children: shares climbed 11.4% on Monday as investors responded to early traction for the company's Muse AI assistant and renewed analyst optimism.

The move followed Wells Fargo's decision to lift its price target to $796 from $640 while maintaining its existing rating. The firm pointed to early adoption of Muse and recent progress across Meta's AI products.

Muse has gained attention shortly after its Sept. 8 launch, reaching the top position on Apple's U.S. App Store. The assistant is designed to handle tasks such as research, form completion and online purchases, giving investors an early indication of consumer interest in Meta's agent-focused AI strategy.

The rally also came ahead of Meta Connect, which starts Wednesday. Investors are expected to watch for additional AI product updates and indications of how the company could develop revenue streams around its growing AI portfolio.
Monday's advance added to a broader technology rally, with the Nasdaq Composite gaining 2.3%. Meta's shares have now risen about 35% during September.

title: Meta Stock Soars After Jaw-Dropping Price Target Hike on AI Products
